messages.content: what's the color of the sea?

function.name: generate_sea_foam
function.description: Simulates the creation of sea foam based on the agitation level of water, amount of organic material, and the presence of salt. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

agitation_level.description: The level of agitation in the water, represented by a scale from 1 (calm) to 10 (very agitated).

organic_material.description: The amount of organic material present in grams per liter. This is a float type value.

salt_presence.description: Indicates whether salt is present (true) or not (false) in the water.

temperature.description: The water temperature in degrees Celsius. If unspecified, defaults to average sea temperature. This is a float type value.

message.content: The color of the sea can vary widely depending on factors such as depth, clarity, the presence of algae or plankton, and the angle of sunlight. In general, clear ocean water appears blue because water absorbs longer wavelengths (red, orange, yellow) and scatters shorter wavelengths (blue). Near the surface, especially in shallow waters, you might see a turquoise or greenish hue due to scattering of light and the presence of phytoplankton. In deeper or more turbid waters, the color can shift toward darker blues or even black. So while the classic image is a bright blue, the actual color is a dynamic spectrum ranging from deep indigo to bright turquoise, depending on environmental conditions.
